elements.name: The Stone Path
elements.description: A path of pale stones crosses the garden: the place where every journey begins.
elements.symbolism: The journey as an image of life: a way is made by walking it, one stone at a time.

elements.name: The Olive Tree of Peace
elements.description: An ancient olive tree, its crown silvered, planted when you discovered the greeting of peace.
elements.symbolism: The olive tree: a Mediterranean plant of peace and patience. It grows slowly and endures through generations.

elements.name: The Fountain of Sister Water
elements.description: A stone fountain with clear water, kindled by the morning sun.
elements.symbolism: "Sister Water, who is useful and humble and precious and chaste": in the Canticle, water is a sister to be thanked.

elements.name: The Roses of San Damiano
elements.description: A rose bush flowering beside the wall: it grows where someone has cared for others.
elements.symbolism: Beauty born of service: charity makes barren places flower.

elements.name: The Shared Vegetable Garden
elements.description: Small beds of herbs and vegetables, tended in turn: humble work that nourishes everyone.
elements.symbolism: Daily service: whoever cultivates the garden does not possess it, but keeps it for those who will come.

elements.name: The Cypress of Silence
elements.description: A tall, straight cypress marking the boundary between the garden and the wood.
elements.symbolism: Prayer as a vertical line: roots in the earth, its tip turned toward heaven.

elements.name: The Chaffinches' Nest
elements.description: Among the safest branches, a pair of chaffinches has chosen the garden for its nest.
elements.symbolism: Welcome: the garden becomes home even for those who arrive from beyond it.

elements.name: The Stone Bench
elements.description: A stone bench beneath the wall at noon: a place to sit and remain.
elements.symbolism: Faith as a trusting pause: we do not always have to walk; sometimes we simply remain.

elements.name: The Sunflowers of Thanksgiving
elements.description: A row of sunflowers turning to follow the light through the day.
elements.symbolism: Gratitude: turning toward the light is a daily discipline of the gaze.

elements.name: The Bees' Hive
elements.description: A wooden hive carries the scent of wax; bees come and go among the garden flowers.
elements.symbolism: Fraternity: no bee makes honey alone, and no bee possesses the comb.

steps.text: Lift your gaze from the garden toward the sky. Remain silent for a little while, doing nothing.
Read slowly the opening of the Canticle of the Creatures.
Francis calls the sun "brother" and the moon "sister". What difference would it make to look upon the world as a family rather than as a resource?
If you wish, write in your journal one thing for which today you can say: "Praised be You, my Lord".
Draw near to the fountain. Listen to the sound of water for a few breaths, without haste.
Read again the praise of God written at La Verna: a prayer that asks for nothing.
The Praises of God contain no requests: only recognition. When was the last time you gave thanks without asking for anything?
If you wish, write in your journal three things received today, however small.
Walk the stone path slowly, noticing each step: its weight, its contact, its rhythm.
Read Francis's answer to Brother Leo, who was seeking the right choice.
To Brother Leo, Francis gives no instructions but freedom: "follow your conscience before God". What does this way of accompanying another teach you?
If you wish, write in your journal about a decision you are carrying, and where you feel your conscience turning.
